newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SEC sues over alledged securities defrauding.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SEC sues over alledged securities defrauding.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday it sued two men, a Bahamian company and a Florida corporation for defrauding investors from New Hampshire, Indiana and a group of 20 cadets at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point.
The civil suit, filed in Manhattan federal court, alleges that the defendants fraudulently obtained more than $2.1 million since 1993 in a scheme involving fictitious "prime bank" securities.
The defendants in the suit are: Joseph Bremont of Florida, Jimmy Sanchez of Texas; Comcar International Ltd, a Bahamian company and Commercial Capital Resources, a Florida corporation.
The suit alleges that the defendants falsely represented to investors that they would use their funds to buy and sell bogus "prime bank securities" that would yield enormous profits.
